questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How a type of cow is helping to prevent wildfires in Spain
Famous animals from children's TV shows
Why Spanish farmers are keeping fewer cows
How firefighters are trained in Spain
questions.why: They discuss how cows are helping to stop wildfires in Spain.

questions.q: Why does Beth mention TV shows like Lassie and Flipper?
options: Because she worked on those shows
To show that TV animals are unrealistic
To talk about her favourite childhood pets and the shows she watched
To introduce the idea of animals helping people in trouble
questions.why: The animal stars came to the rescue of humans, and the programme is about real animals helping people.

questions.q: What picture does Beth have in her head, and what does Neil say?
options: A cow running away from a fire – Neil says that's exactly right
A cow in a firefighter's helmet – Neil says 'not quite'
A dog putting out a fire – Neil laughs
A farmer on a horse – Neil agrees
questions.why: Beth imagines a cow wearing a fireman's helmet, and Neil replies, 'Not quite, Beth.'

questions.q: Why are today's wildfires more intense than before?
options: There are more people living and building homes in the forests
Firefighters have less money
Temperatures are rising because of climate change
Farmers burn more grass
questions.why: Neil says increasing temperatures caused by climate change make today's wildfires more intense.

questions.q: According to reporter Craig Langran, why are Spanish forests more likely to catch fire?
options: The trees are too old
Too few animals eat the plants, so the vegetation grows very thick
People leave rubbish in the forests
It rains much less in the forests than it does in the towns and cities
questions.why: He says forests grew unchecked without enough animals to eat them, and dense vegetation catches fire more easily.

questions.q: According to Pablo Schapira, why have big grazing animals like bison and wild horses gone?
options: Because of wildfires
Because they moved to other countries with more space and food
Because there was not enough grass
Because of extinction and domestication
questions.why: He says they are gone from the ecosystem 'because of extinction, domestication'.

questions.q: What do we learn about the tauros cows?
options: They only eat fresh grass
They are kept on farms at night
They are similar to an extinct wild cow and eat over 30 kilos a day
They were brought to Spain from Africa to help farmers in the mountains
questions.why: Tauros are similar to the extinct aurochs, and each eats over 30 kilos a day.

questions.q: Apart from eating, how else do the cows help reduce fires?
options: They walk over plants and dead trees, opening up the forest
They drink lots of water from the rivers, so the ground stays wet
They warn people when there is smoke
They pull fallen trees out of the forest
questions.why: Craig says their trampling helps open up the forest so it's less packed with flammable vegetation.
